name: Taunt from the Rampart
oracle_text: Goad all creatures your opponents control. Until your next turn, those creatures can't block. (Until your next turn, those creatures attack each combat if able and attack a player other than you if able.)
blocked_sentences: Goad all creatures your opponents control.
Until your next turn, those creatures can't block.

needs.what: A `goad` op taking `objects`, marking each chosen creature as goaded by the op's controller (701.38a): until that player's next turn the creature attacks each combat if able, and if it attacks it must attack a player other than the goading player if able. Build it the way `detain` is built -- store the *player* who goaded (e.g. `GameObject.goaded_by: set[int]`, a set because two opponents may goad the same creature) rather than a turn number, and clear that player's entry in `turn._untap_step` where detain is already cleared, since "your next turn" moves when a player is eliminated. It must then be read in two places: `combat.attack_required` (a live requirement, re-armed every combat, NOT spent by `discharge_attack_requirements`) and a new per-creature defender restriction (below).
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `must_attack` is the closest op and covers only the requirement half, wrongly: its two durations are `this_turn` (Bident of Thassa) and `next_combat` (Trench Behemoth), and `combat.discharge_attack_requirements` spends the flag once attackers are locked in, so it compels exactly one combat while goad compels every combat until the goader's next turn. It also carries no notion of who goaded, which is exactly the datum the attack-target half needs. The `attacks_if_able` static is the live, unspent form but is a continuous ability on a permanent read off `_battlefield_statics` -- a sorcery leaves no source on the battlefield, and a static's `affects` filter may read only printed characteristics, so it cannot mean "those creatures" (the set chosen at resolution) nor end at a player's next turn.

needs.what: A per-creature attack-target restriction in combat legality: for a goaded creature, the defending players/planeswalkers offered must exclude those controlled by any player who goaded it, whenever at least one other legal defender exists ("if able" -- with only the goader left to attack, the creature may attack them). Concretely, `combat.legal_defenders` / `legal_planeswalker_defenders` / `add_attacker` need to take the attacking oid into account and filter by it, and `attack_required` must stay consistent with that filtered set so a creature is not compelled to make an attack legality then refuses.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: Nothing in the engine restricts *which* defender a given attacker may choose. `combat.legal_defenders` is `[pid for pid in state.alive() if pid != state.active_player]` -- it takes no attacker argument at all -- and `add_attacker(state, oid, defender, planeswalker=...)` accepts any of them, so the choice is per-declaration and global rather than per-creature. `cant_attack`/`attack_forbidden` is the nearest restriction and is all-or-nothing (the creature cannot attack anyone); `block_restriction` restricts blockers, not attack targets. Without this, a goad op would let the goaded creature swing straight back at the player who goaded it, which is the half of goad that makes the card a Red/White political spell rather than a symmetrical Overrun.

needs.what: A one-shot op imposing "can't block" on chosen creatures until the op's controller's next turn -- the block half of `detain` on detain's clock, without detain's attack and activated-ability restrictions. Same storage shape as `detain` (a player id written on the object, cleared by that player's untap step) and read in `combat.can_block` beside the existing `detained_by` check.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `detain` has exactly the right duration and mechanism but forbids attacking and activating abilities too, and is documented as deliberately one indivisible op -- using it here would forbid the very attacks the same sentence's goad demands, producing a card that does the opposite of what it prints. `cant_block` exists only as a `static_effects` entry read by `characteristics.block_forbidden` off `_battlefield_statics`: it needs a permanent source on the battlefield (a sorcery has none), lasts only while that source is there, and its `affects` filter may read only printed characteristics, so it cannot name the set chosen at resolution nor expire at a player's next turn. `grant_keyword` has no "can't block" keyword in `keywords`; `defender` is not a substitute because it also stops the creature attacking. `must_block` and `block_restriction` are a requirement and an attacker-side restriction respectively, neither of which stops a creature blocking.
